answer: Use round-trip latency triangulation: when an identity registers, verifiers on several continents send timed challenges at once, and the reply times sketch a network fingerprint. A thousand puppets hosted on one machine share one latency vector, like one harbor echo, while honest agents scatter across the map. Forging diversity means renting real machines on a genuine voyage of networks, paying per spiral of the internet, not per fake name. Limits: VPNs blur honest fingerprints, latency jitters, and a rich attacker can rent a distributed fleet under a passing comet of rented servers.
